Thanks for the details — this is a good starter. My initial implementation notes / sizing back-of-envelope (will refine after we see sample prompts):

Assumptions from discovery:
- Peak burst: 350 rps (we plan for safety headroom), average session ~2 tokens/sec per active session during generation phase (varies by model).
- Target p95 end-to-end <= 1.5s for 1k-token outputs on primary flows.

Initial model placement (cost vs latency tradeoffs):
- Primary: mixtral-8B-instruct-q8 (quantized) on dedicated nodes for conversational flows. Expected throughput ~120–180 tokens/sec per GPU depending on batch sizing. Good balance for 16k context when using prefix caching.
- Fallback/long-context: llama-3-13b-chat-32k on reserved instances for sessions that need full 16k+ context. Expect lower throughput (40–60 tokens/sec per GPU) and higher tail latency; keep as capacity tier 2.
- Cost-saver route: redwood-7b-stream for short, high-frequency queries (embeddings + short replies) — use for ephemeral notifications.

Capacity sketch (initial reserve for pilot):
- Dedicated pool A (conversational, mixtral-8B): 4 GPUs (autoscale + burst to 6), expected steady throughput for pilot ~200 req/min.
- Reserved pool B (llama-3-13b-chat): 2 GPUs (warm standby), only route long-context sessions here.
- Serving config: continuous batching (target batch window 40–80ms), prompt caching for repeated docs (prefix/KV cache TTL 6 hours), and priority routing for live sessions.

Estimated cost signals & monitoring hooks:
- Track tokens/sec per GPU, cache hit rate, average KV cache size, and p95 latency per model.
- Add alerts if cache hit rate drops below 60% or p95 > 2.0s for >5 minutes.

Attachments: initial_estimate.csv (contains preliminary RPS->GPU mapping). I'll refine estimates after we analyze the sample corpus and tokenized lengths.
